pct_usage_quote: The PCT is an assessment tool that helps understand cycling trends by using information from the 2011 census. It analyses how people travel to work and school, highlighting the most likely routes for cycling.
how_pct_was_used: The PCT was used to model cycling trends, forecast potential cycling trips for work and school journeys under different scenarios, and identify popular cycling routes to inform the development of the LCWIP cycling network.
length_of_cycle_network_proposed: 10 primary cycling routes (approx. 45kms) 11 secondary and 12 link cycling routes (approx. 42kms)
other_tools_developed: Sustrans 2023 Paths for Everyone Cost calculator, Healthy Streets Assessment Toolkit, and a prioritisation matrix based on 11 quality criteria and AMAT (Active Mode Appraisal Toolkit) scores.
other_tools_used: ["DataShine Commute Tool", "Active Travel England Uplifts Tool", "Active Mode Appraisal Toolkit (AMAT)", "Cycle and Foot Uplift Tool (CFUT)", "Healthy Streets Assessment Toolkit"]
specific_evidence_of_impact: The 2023 public engagement exercise resulted in alterations to the emerging LCWIP network, including the addition of a new northwest corridor (10) and significant changes to corridors 1 and 3.
